chunks: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Abu Thabit from Hanan ibn Sadir from Ibn Abi Ya'fur from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar said:

A freedman (mawla) of Ali (peace be upon him) died, so he said: 'Look if you find an heir for him.' It was said to him: 'Two daughters in al-Yamamah, who were enslaved.' So he purchased them from the deceased's wealth, then handed over the remainder of the inheritance to them.

key_terms.مَوْلًى: Freedman or client of a master, often referring to the freedmen of the Imams

ai.seo_question: How is the inheritance of a mawla of the Imams handled if his heirs are enslaved?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from the chain of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) demonstrates the practical application of *kitabah* (manumission contract) principles, where the estate is used to purchase enslaved relatives to secure their inheritance rights. It highlights the juristic nuance that enslaved individuals can inherit from their masters if freed, emphasizing the fluidity of status in Shia inheritance law. This case serves as a foundational precedent for resolving conflicts between free and enslaved heirs in the absence of other free descendants.
